title: Forever Add-on Catalog
description: The add-ons Forever Add-on Manager can find and install for WoW Forever. Rules the schema can't express (unique IDs, references between entries, folders claimed twice) are checked by scripts/validate.cs.

$schema.description: Optional link to this schema, for editors.

schemaVersion.description: The format version. The app refuses a catalog whose schemaVersion it doesn't know.

version.description: The catalog's own version, bumped whenever entries change, so the app can say what's new.

id.description: Lowercase letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens. Stable: never changed, never reused.

tag.description: One of the catalog's tags. Adding one is a schema change, so the app can give it an icon at the same time.

folder.description: A top-level AddOns folder. No paths and no leading dot.

tocPath.description: The .toc to read the Interface from, relative to the zip's top level, with forward slashes ("Questie_Forever.toc" or "OpenMap/OpenMap.toc").

forever.description: The WoW Forever client the catalog was checked against. Updated by hand when the client patches.

repo.description: owner/name. The release GitHub flags as Latest is used, never a pre-release.

assetPattern.description: Regular expression (.NET) the release asset's file name must match.

excludePattern.description: Regular expression (.NET) for asset names to skip even when assetPattern matches.

downloadPage.description: The page where the player downloads the Forever release by hand: the project's files page, filtered to the right game version when CurseForge allows it. Only when the project's front page would lead to the wrong file.

downloadHint.description: How to recognise the Forever download on that page, for the player ("the file whose name ends in -forever"). Only when the page alone doesn't make it clear.

downloadPage.description: The page where the player downloads the Forever release by hand: the add-on's versions page, filtered to the right game version when Wago allows it. Only when the add-on's front page would lead to the wrong file.

downloadHint.description: How to recognise the Forever download on that page, for the player ("the file whose name ends in -forever"). Only when the page alone doesn't make it clear.

withdrawn.description: A release the app never offers.

release.description: The release as the source names it: a GitHub tag, a CurseForge file ID or a Wago release.

override.description: Changes that apply from a given release on, for when an add-on adds or renames a folder or moves its .toc.

author.description: One name: the add-on's main author, or the owner of its listing on its first source. Not a list or a group.

summary.description: One sentence in our own words, not copied from the add-on's page.

tags.description: From the fixed list (schema/README.md). The first is the add-on's main tag: the app shows its icon when the add-on has none.

added.description: The day the entry joined the catalog (YYYY-MM-DD), for sorting by date added. Optional in the format, but the validator requires it on a new entry in a PR.

repository.description: The public GitHub or GitLab repository that holds the add-on's source code, whatever its licence. Never one that only hosts issues. Left out when the code isn't public.

issues.description: Where players report problems to the author: the repository's issues when it has them turned on, else the tracker the author links from their CurseForge or Wago page. Left out when there isn't a working one.

sponsor.description: Every page where the author asks for support, as the author lists them, most preferred first: their GitHub Sponsors page, the links in FUNDING.yml, the Donate button on their CurseForge or Wago page, then the other support links they list there. Left out when the author lists none.

icon.description: A small square image (PNG or JPEG) for the add-on, from its author's own repository or add-on page, only where that site's terms allow showing it in another app. Left out otherwise; the app shows a placeholder.

requires.description: Catalog IDs that must be installed too.

optional.description: Catalog IDs it works with when they're installed.

conflicts.description: Catalog IDs it overlaps with. A warning, not a blocker.
